title: Preparing Biological Samples for Column Chemistry
author: Alexis Wasson
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.fqhbmt6

steps.title: Prepare Oxalate Wash
steps.instruction: Prepare an oxalate wash to remove extracellular iron from diatoms by mixing reagents in 600 ml of ultra pure water.

substeps.instruction: Add 15.3g EDTA, 14.7g Sodium Citrate, 0.74g Potassium Chloride, and 5g Sodium Chloride.
Add several drops of Sodium Hydroxide until a pH of 6-7 is reached.
Add 12.6g Oxalic Acid.
Add ultra pure water until the total volume reaches 1 L once pH 8 is reached.

steps.title: Prepare Filtration Materials
steps.instruction: Gather and prepare all necessary equipment for harvesting diatoms.

substeps.instruction: Clean tweezers and polycarbonate filters (0.1um) in 10% HCl overnight; rinse filters in UPW.
Prepare three bottles: one for waste, one containing ASW, and one containing UPW.
Prepare a 60ml syringe and syringe filter tip.
Label 15ml tubes for 'unwashed' and 'washed' solutions (e.g., 'solution 1#1 unwashed', 'solution 1#2 washed').

steps.title: Filter Unwashed Culture
steps.instruction: Harvest the initial portion of the culture to obtain unwashed samples.

substeps.instruction: Using polyethylene gloves, place a polycarbonate filter on the filter rig and screw on the reservoir.
Rinse the filter with UPW.
Pour 250ml of culture (grown to approximately 3500 RFU) onto the filter and allow it to drain.
Rinse the filter three times with 5ml of ASW.
Remove the filter with tweezers and place it in the corresponding 'unwashed' 15ml tube.

steps.title: Filter Washed Culture
steps.instruction: Treat the remaining culture with oxalate wash and filter to obtain washed samples.

substeps.instruction: Syringe filter 60ml of oxalate wash into the remaining 750ml of culture.
Invert the bottle once and let sit for 30min, then invert a second time.
Place a new polycarbonate filter on the rig and rinse with UPW.
Pour the remaining culture onto the filter.
Rinse the filter three times with 5ml ASW and drain completely.
Remove the filter and place it in the corresponding 'washed' 15ml tube.
Repeat the process for all 1L bottles.

steps.title: Clean Filtration Apparatus
steps.instruction: Clean all equipment used during filtration.

substeps.instruction: Rinse tweezers and the filter rig with UPW.
Rinse bottles with UPW and move to the clean lab for final cleaning.

steps.title: Acid Digestion of Filters
steps.instruction: Digest the filters to release iron for isotopic analysis.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the filter from the 15ml tube into a small Teflon (PFA) vial.
Add 1 mL conc. TE clean HCl and 1 mL conc. TE clean HNO3 to each vial.
Place caps loosely on vials and store in a fume hood overnight (do not apply heat if using a hot plate).

steps.title: Recover Iron and Evaporate
steps.instruction: Recover the diatoms and associated iron from the acid digestion.

substeps.instruction: Remove filters from vials using Teflon tweezers, ensuring most diatom shells remain on the filter.
Rinse the filter twice by pipetting 1 mL of TE H2O over the filter back into the PFA vial to recover Fe.
Evaporate the samples to dryness on a hot plate.

steps.title: Sample Reconstitution and Column Purification
steps.instruction: Reconstitute samples and purify using mini columns.

substeps.instruction: Reconstitute samples in 200 uL of 10N HCl + 0.001% H2O2.
Collect a subsample.
Run samples through 135 uL 'mini' columns according to established procedures.
While columns run, clean PFA vials by blasting with TE water and heating with 0.1 N HNO3 for 1-2 hours.
Elute from columns back into the original PFA vials.

steps.title: Final Sample Processing
steps.instruction: Concentrate and dilute the purified samples for elemental analysis.

substeps.instruction: Dry down samples overnight (or for a few hours).
Redissolve in 100ul of conc. HNO3.
Cap and place on a hot plate in the bio lab for 30min at 350 degrees.
Move to the biological lab hot plate to dry down further.
Reconstitute in 1100ul 0.1N HNO3.
Take 100ul of this sample, dilute to 1ml with 0.1N HNO3, and place in a 15ml vial for elemental analysis.

steps.title: Isotopic Spike Addition
steps.instruction: Prepare the final sample for isotopic analysis based on iron concentration.

substeps.instruction: Calculate the amount of Fe in each sample based on the elemental analysis results.
Add enough double-spike to achieve a 1:2 sample:spike ratio.
